welcome_lead: Explore the Islamic duties of giving to charity and fasting in Ramadan.

walkthroughs.body_html: Zakah is the third Pillar. Muslims who can afford it give 2.5% of their savings each year to the poor and to good causes. It reminds Muslims that all wealth comes from God and should be shared.

Sawm is the fourth Pillar — fasting during Ramadan, the ninth month of the Islamic calendar. From dawn to sunset, Muslims do not eat, drink, smoke or argue. Fasting builds self-discipline and reminds Muslims of those who are hungry.
During Ramadan, Muslims wake before dawn for suhoor (early meal) and break the fast at sunset with iftar, often starting with dates and water. Ramadan ends with the celebration of Eid al-Fitr.

mcqs.q: How did Hume define a miracle?
options: Hume defined a miracle as something amazing or unexpected.
Hume believed all miracles in the Bible really happened.
A violation of the laws of nature by a particular volition of the Deity — and he argued evidence for such violations could never outweigh the uniform experience supporting the laws.
Because Jesus was crucified, and the Messiah cannot die.

mcqs.q: Why do Jews not accept Jesus as the Messiah?
options: Because Jesus was crucified, and the Messiah cannot die.
Hume believed all miracles in the Bible really happened.
Because Jews believe Jesus never existed.
Because the Jewish Messiah is expected to bring peace, rebuild the Temple and restore Israel — events the Jewish tradition holds Jesus did not accomplish.
